newsitem.title: GERMANY: ANALYSTS' VIEW - Mega-merger by Bavarian banks.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSTS' VIEW - Mega-merger by Bavarian banks.

text.p: The following are analysts' reactions to the merger plans announced on Monday by Bavaria's Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechsel- Bank AG to create Germany's second largest bank.

"We are pleased to see that the consolidation in the German banking sector has started sooner rather than later. However we are a little surprised by several aspects such as the limited scale of staff cuts indicated (5,000 to 7,000 according to industry sources). And I think the savings planned (one billion marks in five years) are a little optimistic based on that sort of staffing. I also think the plan to spread savings over five years could have been more aggressive, there appears to be some kind of political pressure here in association with the 'Bavarian solution'. So basically we are a little sceptical."
(Salomon has cut Vereinsbank to hold from buy on the news)
"Vereinsbank shares have had a very nice movement. They have risen 90 percent in the last 12 months. I think the best is already in the Vereinsbank share."
"This is the first major merger in the German banking sector. It means the speculation about future merger moves can only continue, particularly for smaller banks.
"I think what we have now is the solution for Bavaria. What will be interesting now is what happens elsewhere. (Hein has issued a buy recommendation on the banking sector)
"It seems that Vereinsbank was the driving force behind this. It saw that it could not survive independently and it took action.
"The good point is that this will be accomplished in a shareholder value friendly manner. The number of shares will be reduced by this action, which will benefit earnings per share.
(Hein sees the new bank having 430 million shares in circulation. Hypo now has 257 million and Vereinsbank 265 million).
"In the second place the savings plan for one billion marks a year is very positive.
"On the negative side, both banks remain weak in investment banking. The merger cannot convert a double weakness into a strength. Something will have to be done here."
